manualReview.note: Worker inspected logs and actual before/after PNGs from the root-owned existing manual replay; no generation or browser launched by reviewer.

label: prototype

controls.label: Trigger sprayer: arrow keys squeeze and release the trigger, space toggles auto pump
controls.reason: Supported End key moves the piston from rest to full squeeze, compresses the spring and moves the trigger; readout changes from Rest/cylinder full to Held/both valves shut. The source End handler sets trigger=100 and disables auto pump, so the geometry is input-caused rather than ambient settling.

oldIdentity.label: Trigger sprayer: arrow keys squeeze and release the trigger, space toggles auto pump

controls.label: Spray
controls.reason: The before frame shows a narrow stream with Stream selected; the additionally inspected after1 frame shows a broad spray cone with Spray selected. Source nozzle-mode handler changes spread from 0.02 to 0.36; auto pumping supplies the squeeze, and the mode-specific pattern proves this control despite moving pixels failing the static threshold.

controls.label: Stream
controls.reason: Before shows the broad spray droplets and Spray selected; after0 shows a narrow contiguous stream with Stream selected. The source stream branch changes particle spread/radius/speed, matching the visible pattern. Later after1 is the refill phase, explaining why persistent-pixel scoring remains unproven.

controls.label: Off
controls.reason: Off stops ejection and restores the trigger while both after frames display Nozzle shut / water cannot compress / trigger is stuck. This is the source nozzle-off hydraulic lock branch, not merely selected-button styling; automatic pump remains enabled.

controls.label: Seat belt retractor: arrow keys change braking in g, M switches between car braking and belt yank
controls.reason: Supported Home key changes braking from 0.80 g (locked by pendulum after 22 mm) to 0.00 g (free, 0 mm out), with the pendulum and pawl visibly returning. Source Home sets zero and reduced-motion settles the model deterministically, so the change is not autonomous timing or focus outline.

oldIdentity.label: Seat belt retractor: arrow keys change braking in g, M switches between car braking and belt yank

controls.label: Toaster: Space presses the lever, arrow keys set browning
controls.reason: Stage click invokes the supported press/cancel handler. Before shows popped bread with lever raised; after shows bread lowered, compressed spring, hot element and active strip temperature/time. This is a new toast cycle started by the click, not focus styling.

oldIdentity.label: Toaster: Space presses the lever, arrow keys set browning

controls.label: tw-browning
controls.reason: Browning drag changes dial 2 to 5.5, visibly rotates the drawn dial and moves the trip stop; predicted next pop time changes from about 1:23 to 3:30 and remains 3:30 in after1. Previous pop time stays 1:23, so the new prediction is caused by browning rather than ongoing heating.

controls.label: B-tree lookup: arrow keys pick the id, i toggles the index
controls.reason: Supported ArrowRight changes lookup id from 420,000 to 530,000, updates the explanation and highlights a different leaf/table route. Source increments normalized key by 11; reduced-motion uses the final lookup state, excluding an autonomous tour.

oldIdentity.label: B-tree lookup: arrow keys pick the id, i toggles the index

controls.label: No index
controls.reason: No index click changes B-tree 4 page reads to Full scan 10,000 page reads and rewrites the explanation. Body height shrinks, but actual calculated output changes, matching the index=false branch.

controls.label: B-tree index
controls.reason: B-tree index click changes Full scan 10,000 pages to 4 page reads and restores the index-path explanation and visible highlighted route. This is the supported index=true branch, not selected-button appearance.

controls.label: Rows in table, powers of ten
controls.reason: Rows slider changes 10 thousand to 100 million rows; output changes from 3 to 5 index page reads, hypothetical scan from 100 to 1,000,000, and lookup id from 4,200 to 42,000,000. The size/read-count model matches these changes despite text wrapping and card resize.

controls.label: Merge bench: keys 1 to 4 cycle each hunk, M toggles whether main moved
controls.reason: Real-input request20 presses supported key 1 on the stage. The before/after PNGs show hunk1 feature and result blocks changing A to B while the unrelated conflict remains. Logs confirm hunk1 none→feature; the persistent drawn output proves the stage despite generic unsupported probes failing.

oldIdentity.label: Merge bench: keys 1 to 4 cycle each hunk, M toggles whether main moved

controls.replayReason: Before/after geometry and state are unchanged. Source exposes only digit keys 1–4 and M on this stage; generic drag/click/Home/End/arrows/Space/Enter never invoke its handler. This is unsupported input coverage, not evidence of a dead stage. Prepared request20 uses key1.

controls.label: WebSocket chat: Enter sends a message, M switches between WebSocket and polling, arrows change the poll interval
controls.reason: Supported stage click adds a third message line to all three client pads (two before, three in both after images). Source click invokes send and reduced-motion disables automatic touring, so the added bubbles are causal message delivery. The automatic semantic gate misses opacity-revealed SVG message paths.

oldIdentity.label: WebSocket chat: Enter sends a message, M switches between WebSocket and polling, arrows change the poll interval

controls.label: WebSocket
controls.reason: WebSocket click changes polling average/worst 1.6/3.1 s and 20 requests/min to 100/100 ms and zero polling requests, restores open wires, hides interval and shows completed handshake. These model outputs directly match mode=websocket.

controls.label: Polling
controls.reason: Polling click changes 100ms delivery and zero polls to 1.6s average, 3.1s worst and 20 requests/min; exposes interval and explains timed polling. Actual outputs change even though card height grows.

controls.label: latency
controls.reason: Latency drag changes one-way 50 to 270 ms; average delivery changes 1.6 to 2.0 s and worst case 3.1 to 3.5 s while interval stays 3s and request rate stays 20. This is the model latency effect, not autonomous packet traffic.

controls.label: interval
controls.reason: Request23 enables Polling, sets #interval to Home then End with real keys. Inspected PNGs change interval 1→15 s, independent average delivery 600 ms→7.6 s and requests/min 60→4; latency stays 50 ms. Both after logs retain the new readout, proving the previously unexercised conditional control.
controls.replayReason: Poll interval appears after mode selection; the replay retains its identity but never drives it. Visually inspected Polling after image confirms the visible 3s input. Source needs polling mode before #interval is meaningful. Prepared request23 changes Home to End while polling.

controls.label: Load balancer figure: left and right arrows change the algorithm, up and down change the traffic
controls.reason: Supported ArrowRight changes algorithm from Round robin to Least-connections in the independent model readout. The source key handler updates algo and pick() consults it. Queue evolution is visible but is not used alone as causal proof because traffic runs continuously.

oldIdentity.label: Load balancer figure: left and right arrows change the algorithm, up and down change the traffic

controls.label: Round robin
controls.reason: Round robin click changes the model readout from Least-connections to Round-robin, beyond selected-button styling. The source handler feeds the actual dispatch pick() branch. Simultaneous queue/average changes are not independently attributed to the click.

controls.label: Least connections
controls.reason: Least connections click changes the model readout from Round-robin to Least-connections. Source maps this parameter to minimum-open-connections dispatch; readout change is causal, while the moving queue is treated as background rather than standalone proof.

controls.label: Random
controls.reason: Random click changes the model readout from Round-robin to Random. Source dispatch pick() uses the selected random branch; no automatic cycling changes the algorithm. Changing queue counts alone is not counted as proof.

controls.label: rate
controls.reason: Fresh-page equal-time requests25/26 use Round robin and 4x Server C slowdown, changing only traffic through real Home/End input. At ~20.02/~20.01 s, inspected PNGs show open connections A/B/C=1/0/1 at 0.5 req/s versus 8/7/8 at 4 req/s, average 2.6→6.9 s, drops 0→19. Logs corroborate the contrast at 10 and 15 s. This isolates a substantial modeled load effect beyond the slider and autonomous aging of one run.
controls.replayReason: Slider moves from about 1.2 to 3.5 requests/s, but the observed queue/count/latency changes also occur autonomously under Random routing. Screenshots do not isolate a traffic-rate effect beyond input chrome. Prepared fresh-page equal-time requests25/26 compare low and high rate under fixed Round robin.

controls.label: slow
controls.reason: Fresh-page equal-time requests27/28 hold Round robin and 4 req/s constant, changing only slowdown via real Home/End. At ~10.01/~10.02 s, inspected PNGs show identical A/B=5/6 but C=6 versus 8 and drops=0 versus 2; at ~20.02/~20.01 s the inspected drop counts are 9 versus 19 (averages 6.7 versus 6.9 s). This repeatable Server C pressure difference proves live service-time input beyond autonomous queue motion.
controls.replayReason: Server C slowdown slider changes about 1.5x to 3.5x, while all queues, average latency and drop count keep evolving. This short Random-routing pair cannot isolate changed service time from autonomous traffic. Prepared requests27/28 compare min/max slowdown at equal elapsed times under fixed rate and Round robin.

controls.label: Daily digest
controls.reason: Daily digest click removes the time picker and the daily-digest clause from the explanatory sentence. The screenshot pair confirms real output despite card shrink, matching the digest parameter handler.

controls.label: Send digest at
controls.reason: Request22 starts from fresh digest-enabled state and uses real keys on the visible time select. The inspected pair changes the separate summary from daily digest at 7 AM to 9 AM; both after logs confirm digest remains enabled and digestTime=9. The former failure was the earlier trial hiding the select.
controls.replayReason: Both screenshots show Daily digest off, so the Send digest at select is hidden. The earlier toggle hid it before its trial. Source condition digest=true reveals it and summary uses digestTime; this replay never exercised that prerequisite. Prepared request22 starts from the fresh page with digest enabled and changes the select.
